blocks.text: Anyone flying out of Kathmandu’s Tribhuvan International Airport on an Indian-registered aircraft undergoes an additional security screening just before boarding. At a screening point on a raised platform on the airport apron, staffed by Indian security personnel, passengers are frisked, and their luggage is subjected to a thorough hand search. It’s hardly a secret; nor is it new. But after more than a quarter of a century, it is simply part of boarding.
